story: You're at home and not on Wi-Fi. WhatsApp shows a little clock next to every message you send, and YouTube won't play anything.
You came back from a flight this morning. Hours later, nothing on the phone that needs the internet is working.
The Wi-Fi symbol at the top of your phone is full, but every website just keeps loading and loading.
At a friend's house your phone joined their Wi-Fi without trouble, yet no app can get anything to load.
Your daughter says she called you three times this morning. Your phone was next to you and made no sound.
Since last night, calls only show up later as missed calls. The phone never makes a sound when they come in.
When you answer a call, the timer on the screen is running, but you can't hear the other person at all.
On calls, the other person sounds so faint that you press the phone hard to your ear and still miss what they say.
Your friend says she sent you a message hours ago. It only appeared when you opened the app yourself.
Your email and shopping apps used to show a little alert at the top of the screen. Now you only see anything when you open them.
Your phone has started reading out everything you touch in a robot voice, and one tap doesn't open anything any more.
A green box appears around whatever you touch, and you have to tap twice to open an app.
Everything on your screen has gone grey, like an old black-and-white TV.
Overnight, white pages turned black and your photos look like old film negatives.
Even indoors, your screen is so dark you can hardly read it.
Your grandson played with your phone, and since then the whole screen looks dull and dark.
While you read a long message, the screen goes black after a few seconds unless you keep touching it.
You're following a recipe on the phone, and it keeps going dark and locking while your hands are busy.
You turn the phone on its side to watch a cricket match, but the picture stays upright and small.
Photos used to fill the screen when you held the phone sideways. Now nothing moves when you turn it.
You need your reading glasses for every message. The letters on the phone look tiny.
Names in your contacts and the words in menus look much smaller than on your friend's phone of the same model.
Your wireless earphones are charged and switched on, but the phone doesn't find them.
The speaker at home used to play songs from your phone without wires. Now the phone won't link to it.
In a video call app, the other person can't see you. Where your face should be, there's only a black square.
The maps app keeps saying it can't tell where you are, even though you're standing on a main road.
The clock on your phone is an hour behind, and you turned up late because of it.
Websites show a warning that your connection isn't private, and the phone says today's date is in 2019.
Wi-Fi, mobile data and Bluetooth all keep failing. A friend says the phone should forget all its connections and start afresh.
The man at the mobile shop said the phone's saved network settings are messed up and need to be wiped clean.
Your phone was fully charged in the morning and is nearly dead by lunchtime.
Apps take ages to open, and the phone freezes for a few seconds every time you type.
The phone won't let you take any more photos. It says there's no space left.
You dropped your phone, and now there's a line running across the screen.
You changed the code that unlocks your phone last week, and now you can't remember it.
You're paying online and waiting for the one-time code from your bank, but it never arrives.
There's a power cut. You want to use the phone as a torch but don't know how.
You need the phone to wake you at 5 tomorrow for an early train.
Your phone has been acting strangely since yesterday, but you can't say exactly what's wrong.
WhatsApp just isn't working for you today, and you're not sure why.
Think of a real problem you once had with your phone. Write the message you'd have typed then.
Another real problem you've had with a phone, yours or someone else's. Write what you'd have typed.
One more: any phone trouble you've had or helped someone with. Write what you'd have typed.
